Scientific Hypothesis: Increased ease of immigration (as captured by the imputed share of immigrant employment) has a negative effect on the local job market for native workers, as indicated by the negative coefficient of -0.00277 and a statistically significant p-value of 0.0002. This suggests that higher levels of immigrant employment may be associated with a decrease in the share of native employment in the local job market.
